main_body: A bare, snow-dusted birch-like tree: a long pale trunk with dark bark marks, thin branches fanning out at the top, and a small snow patch at the base.
top_band: none. The column at x=16 runs from a dark outline (rows 9-10) into one pale trunk tone (L=206) with dark bark marks, with no horizontal top surface.
evidence: The trunk is a tall vertical cylinder drawn straight from the front, in one flat pale tone with dark bark flecks. The branches are thin, mostly 1px lines. There is no cap, ellipse top or canopy surface seen from above, so no horizontal surface reads. For an organic tree the trunk is a thin vertical column with no top-face ellipse, and it matches the flat-band or rim-only failure. There is no 3/4 structure, so it fails.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 9 distinct colours against 427 and 567 for the references. The median colours per full tile is 0 because the piece is smaller than a tile, so I judged by eye. The trunk is a flat pale column of roughly 3 tones with a few neutral black bark marks. All of the dark edge pixels are neutral (100%), where the references' are tinted (0%). The branches are sparse single-pixel lines with no leaf clumps or foliage mass. Beodeul trees carry 5-6 green steps, bark grain and clumped canopies, so the candidate is much thinner and flatter and looks like a sticker next to them. The 5x5 flat-fill coverage measures 0%, but only because the trunk is narrow; the large light trunk surface is still effectively unvaried.
